title: Know every cost: why busy is not the same as profitable

say: Know every cost: why busy is not the same as profitable.
This is the video for Module 1 of Pricing, Costing and Profit Planning.
Many women sell every day and still have nothing to show at the end of the month. Usually the problem is the price, not hard work.
Revenue is all the money customers pay you. 40 bottles at 300 naira is 12,000 naira of revenue.

say: They come to 12,000 naira. Divided by 40, that is 300 naira a bottle, exactly her selling price.

say: So her batch costs 13,500 naira, but sells for only 12,000 naira. She loses about 1,500 naira every batch, before counting her own time.
Selling more would only make the loss bigger.

say: These are the costs most often left out. First, your own labour. If you do not pay yourself, your price is too low.
Packaging and labels, transport to market and to customers, and energy like gas and generator fuel.
Phone data and airtime for WhatsApp orders.
Wastage: burnt batches, broken items and unsold food.
And equipment wear, market dues, and POS and transfer charges.
Sort each cost in two ways. Variable costs rise and fall with how much you make. Make twice as much chin chin, and you use about twice as much flour, oil and packaging.
Direct costs can be traced to one item, like the lining in one gown.
Fixed costs stay about the same each month, like rent, a market levy and your own wage. Indirect costs, or overheads, support the whole business.
Quick test: if I made nothing this month, would I still pay it? If yes, it is fixed.
Halima's monthly overheads are rent, an apprentice, generator fuel and data. Together, 80,000 naira.
The lining, zip, thread, interfacing and buttons for one gown cost 4,400 naira.
Shared across 40 garments, each one carries 2,000 naira of overheads.
So each gown costs 6,400 naira before she pays herself. If she charged 6,000 naira, she would lose money on every gown.
In a slow month of 20 garments, each would carry 4,000 naira of overheads. Fixed costs do not shrink when sales fall.
Every calculation is only as good as your numbers. Capture every receipt for two weeks, with the quantity as well as the price. Weigh and count real batches.
Measure your wastage, keep business money in a separate account, and decide a fair monthly wage for yourself.
Protect your money. Fraudsters send fake screenshots or SMS alerts. Confirm every payment inside your bank app or on your POS before you release goods.

cards.d: Confirm every payment inside your bank or wallet app, or on your POS, before releasing goods.
No genuine bank, POS company or customer needs your PIN, password or one-time code.
Wait until the full amount shows in your app and check it is not reversed before refunding.

say: Never share your PIN, password or one-time code, even with someone who says they are bank staff.

say: If someone overpays and asks for a refund, wait until the full amount shows in your app and is not reversed.
And if a supplier sends new account details, call them on the number you already have before paying.

say: To remember. Profit is revenue minus total cost. Selling more at a loss-making price only makes the loss bigger. Count your labour, packaging, data and wastage. Fixed costs stay, even in slow months. And confirm every payment in your app.
